PAGE 7 – A Lesson from the Silence
When they returned to the classroom, Teacher Mia wrote three words on the board:
“What did we learn today?” she asked.
“We learned that we should listen before we make conclusions.”
Liza added, “We should also ask questions instead of blaming someone.”
“And we should help when we can,” he said softly.
Teacher Mia looked around the classroom.
“This morning, our classroom was noisy. Then it became silent because we were worried. But that silence helped us notice things we usually ignore.”
“We heard the wind. We noticed the rain. We saw the footprints. Most importantly, we listened to Jun’s explanation.”

Sa ilang pagbalik sa classroom, nagsulat si Teacher Mia og tulo ka pulong sa pisara:
“Unsa may atong nakat-unan karon?” iyang pangutana.
“Nakat-on mi nga kinahanglan una ta maminaw sa dili pa maghimo og conclusion.”
Midugang si Liza, “Kinahanglan usab ta mangutana imbes nga mangbasol og tawo.”
Nagtindog si Jun duol sa pultahan.
“Ug kinahanglan ta motabang kung makahimo ta,” hinay niyang giingon.
Mitan-aw si Teacher Mia sa tibuok classroom.
“Kaniadto buntaga, saba ang atong classroom. Dayon nahilom kini kay nabalaka ta. Apan ang maong kahilom nakatabang nato nga mapansin ang mga butang nga kasagarang dili nato tagdon.”
“Nadungog nato ang hangin. Namatikdan nato ang ulan. Nakita nato ang mga tunob. Labaw sa tanan, naminaw ta sa explanation ni Jun.”

They also decided to make a small emergency corner near the classroom door. They labeled the emergency bag clearly and placed a list beside it showing what was inside.
From that day on, the students became more careful.
When someone made a mistake, they asked what happened before blaming them.
When someone needed help, they tried to help.
And whenever the classroom became unusually quiet, the students remembered the Monday when the rain, wind, and missing emergency bag taught them an important lesson.

“Sa dili pa manghusga, MAMINAW UNA TA.”
Nakadesisyon usab sila nga maghimo og gamay nga emergency corner duol sa pultahan sa classroom. Klaro nilang gibutangan og label ang emergency bag ug gibutang ang listahan sa mga sulod niini.
Sukad niadto, mas nahimong maampingon ang mga estudyante.
Kung adunay masayop, ilang pangutan-on una kung unsay nahitabo sa dili pa mangbasol.
Kung adunay nanginahanglan og tabang, ilang paningkamotan nga motabang.

1. Where did the events in the story take place?
2. What happened when the strong wind blew into the classroom?
A. The students immediately went home.
B. The papers flew off the table.
C. The teacher left the classroom.
3. What caused the classroom to become silent?
A. The students were taking an examination.
C. The storm grew stronger, and the electricity went out.
D. The students went outside to play.
4. Why did Jun move the emergency bag?
A. He wanted to hide it from the teacher.
B. He wanted to take it home.
C. He wanted to protect it from the rain coming through the window.
D. He wanted to play with it.

A. Blame others whenever something goes missing.
B. Listen and gather information before judging others.
